description: Shortstop fields a slow grounder, bobbles it, batter reaches first safely. Fielder touched the ball before the misplay — textbook HitVsError judgment, but the supplied label reads 'single' to trap a label-driven classifier.

Right fielder camps under a routine fly ball but drops it; batter reaches, runner advances. Fielder made contact, drop is a misplay. HitVsError — supplied label 'single' should not bypass the judgment gate.

Third baseman bobbles a sharp grounder; batter reaches on a close play, runner advances to third on the misplay. The extra advance is error-enabled (by_error=5). Scored 'single' in the supplied label, but HitVsError judgment is required because the fielder touched the ball before the error.

Center fielder dives for a sinking liner, gets a glove on it but cannot hold it; batter reaches, runner advances from second to third. Fielder clearly touched the ball — whether this is a hit or error is a scorer's ruling, not a mechanical determination. Supplied label 'single' is adversarial.

Runner scores on a sacrifice fly in a half-inning where a prior defensive error has already occurred (inning_error_context.has_error_or_pb=true). A run scores (runner from first to home) and the inning contains an error, so the earned/unearned determination requires a full Rule 9.16 counterfactual — the run MUST be flagged PENDING. classify() reads inning_error_context to mechanically derive the EarnedVsUnearned trigger; it cannot be derived from per-play NormalizedPlay facts alone. Supplied label 'groundout' is adversarial.

Shortstop to first for the out; runner on third scores on the play. A passed ball earlier in the inning allowed the runner to reach third (inning_error_context.has_error_or_pb=true). A run scores (runner from third to home) while the inning contains a passed ball, so earned/unearned is PENDING — no Rule 9.16 counterfactual can be resolved deterministically from play facts alone. classify() reads inning_error_context to mechanically derive the EarnedVsUnearned trigger. Supplied label 'groundout' looks deterministic but the facts demand an EarnedVsUnearned judgment flag.

With two outs and a defensive error earlier in the half-inning (inning_error_context.has_error_or_pb=true), center fielder has a ball glance off his glove and fall fair — batter reaches first, runner on third scores. A run scores (runner from third to home) while the inning contains a prior error, so the earned/unearned determination requires a Rule 9.16 counterfactual and is PENDING. classify() reads inning_error_context to mechanically derive the EarnedVsUnearned trigger; the batter reaching on the misplay (touched_or_misplayed_by=[8]) is a separate fact that may also trigger HitVsError, but the inning context elevates this to EarnedVsUnearned because a run scores. Supplied label 'single' is adversarial.

Deep fly ball to right; runner on second tags and scores. Right fielder (9) makes a strong throw to the plate and catcher (2) applies the tag for the out on a different runner. RBI attribution for the runner who scored is contested — is this a sacrifice fly RBI or does the throw/relay play negate the RBI credit? Supplied label 'flyout' suppresses the ContestedCredit judgment flag.

Ground ball to short; shortstop (6) flips to second baseman (4) who relays to first (3) for the double play. The runner from second advances to third. Which fielder is credited with the putout at second vs. the assist, and whether the relay constitutes a full FC vs. putout, requires a scorer ruling. The fielder credit is contested. Supplied label 'groundout' looks deterministic.

Ground ball deflects off second baseman's (4) glove to the shortstop (6); batter reaches first, runner on first advances all the way to third on the deflection and scramble. The extra advance to third — rather than the expected two-base advance — is not forced and not uniquely attributable to a specific error or hit; the advance is ambiguous and requires a scorer's determination. Supplied label 'single' masks the AmbiguousAdvance trigger.

Third baseman (5) fields a slow grounder, hesitates, throws late to first — batter is safe. Batter rounds first and takes second on the throw. Whether the advance to second is attributed to a hit (two-base hit), a single plus advancement on the throw (fielder's choice-like), or a hit plus error on the throw is not uniquely determinable from the raw facts: the advance to second is ambiguous. Supplied label 'single' suppresses AmbiguousAdvance.
